title: Clocked decrement segment
statement: Let $e$ be an embedding of $\\{0,1\\}$ into an alphabet $\\Gamma$, let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape machine over $\\Gamma$ with state set $S$, and let $\\mathrm{stopAt}:S\\to\\{\\mathrm{false},\\mathrm{true}\\}$. Fix an input word $x$ over $\\Gamma$, a configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, a state $s\\in S$ with $\\mathrm{stopAt}(s)=\\mathrm{false}$, a Boolean word $w$, and a counter tape $ct:\\mathbb Z\\to\\mathrm{Option}(\\Gamma)$ with head position $cp\\in\\mathbb Z$ such that $ct(cp+p)$ contains the symbol of $w$ at offset $p$, mapped through $e$, for every integer $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$ (and is blank where that word has no symbol). Form the clocked machine $H$ from $M$, $e$, and $\\mathrm{stopAt}$, and set $t=2|w\\mathbin{\\mathrm{takeWhile}}(\\mathrm{not})|+2$. After $t$ steps from the clock configuration over $c$ with state recording the decrement phase for $s$ and counter tape $ct$ at $cp$, the machine is in the clock configuration over $c$ with state determined by whether the decrement of $w$ is defined, and counter tape obtained by patching $ct$ at $cp$ with the decremented word mapped through $e$ (using an all-true word of length $|w|$ when the decrement is undefined). This run avoids the finish and timeout states at every time strictly before $t$; at every time from $0$ through $t$, the counter head lies in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and the reached configuration is the clock configuration over the unchanged $c$ with its current counter tape and head position.
